kb_editor_cancel.label: Escape: Finish linking, cancel a pending paste, or drop the selection

kb_editor_cursor.label: Canvas focused: arrow keys move the cursor, Space or Enter paints with the active tool

kb_editor_select.label: S: Select tool. Drag or Shift+arrows select a rectangle; Ctrl (Cmd) + C / X / V copy, cut, paste; Delete clears; Shift+F fills the selection with the chosen palette entry; Alt+arrows or dragging inside the selection move it; Escape cancels a paste or drops the selection

kb_editor_stamps.label: Stamps...: Float a ready-made linked pair (trap and brown button, clone machine and red button, and, on Epoxy rules only, shot trigger and launcher) like a paste; click or press Enter to place it, Shift+R turns it between side by side and stacked

kb_editor_history.label: Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y: Undo / Redo | Ctrl+S: Save

fallback.trap_button: Opens unlinked traps while held (every brown button opens unlinked traps).
fallback.trap_unlinked: No link: any brown button opens it.
fallback.trap_linked: Answers to its linked buttons only.
fallback.clone_any: No link: fires every clone machine with a creature.
fallback.clone_none: No link, and no clone machine holds a creature: fires nothing.

fallback.signal_fires_cloner: Makes one clone each time its linked signal starts sending.

plate.label: Needs a hold door of the same colour ({colour}): this plate opens nothing yet. A hold door opens only while every plate of its colour is pressed.

hold_door.label: Needs a pressure plate of the same colour ({colour}): with no plate it is shut from the start. It opens only while every plate of its colour is pressed.

toggle_button.label: Needs a toggle wall of the same colour ({colour}): this button flips nothing yet. The plain green button flips the plain toggle walls.

toggle_wall.label: Needs a toggle button of the same colour ({colour}): nothing flips this wall yet. The plain green button flips the plain toggle walls.

teleporter_plain.label: Needs another plain teleporter: a plain teleporter sends to the previous plain teleporter in reading order, and alone it goes nowhere.

teleporter_colour.label: Needs another teleporter of the same colour ({colour}): it is alone in its group.

relay_pad.label: Needs another relay pad: a relay pad leads to the other lit relay pads only, and alone it goes nowhere.

laser_receiver.label: Needs a laser gate of the same group ({colour}): this receiver opens nothing yet.

laser_gate.label: Needs a laser receiver of the same group ({colour}): nothing is linked to this gate yet.

puppet_control.label: Needs a puppet: no puppet steps with the player when the player ends a move on this control yet.

puppet.label: Needs a puppet control: puppets step with the player when the player ends a move on a puppet control.

flame_button.label: Needs a flame jet: this orange button toggles nothing yet.

flame_jet.label: Needs an orange button: flame jets are toggled by orange buttons.

cc3d_trap.label: Needs a trap on the level: this trap control opens nothing yet.

cc3d_teleport.label: Needs another {colour} teleport: a teleport sends to the previous teleport of its colour in reading order, and alone it goes nowhere.

cc3d_machine.label: Needs a clone machine: this switch works nothing yet.

cc3d_template.label: Needs a creature or block standing on it: a clone machine copies what stands on it, and this one has nothing to copy.

cc3d_shooter.label: Needs a laser shooter: this controller fires nothing yet.

cc3d_toggle_control.label: Needs a toggle door of the same colour ({colour}): this control flips nothing yet.

cc3d_toggle_door.label: Needs a toggle control of the same colour ({colour}): nothing flips this door yet.

cc3d_golem.label: Needs a {colour} golem: this control moves nothing yet.

cc3d_golem_control.label: Needs a {colour} golem control: a {colour} golem never moves on its own.

trap_uncontrolled.label: No trap control works this trap, so it stays closed.

buried.label: This device is under another layer, so it does nothing: toggle controls, clone switches, laser controllers, golem controls and teleports work only from the top layer of their cell.

behind_cover.label: This device is under a door, socket or false wall: it works only if the player opens that cell and then steps onto it.

keys.label: Keys: K starts or ends linking from the device under the cursor, T tests the level from the cursor, L shows or hides the laser beam preview, Shift+R turns the creature or turret under the cursor or turns a floating stamp, Shift+F fills the selection with the chosen entry.

lynx.label: Lynx levels: only trap and clone links exist, one per button; a brown or red button with no link does nothing, and its trap or clone machine stays shut.

track.name: Track cells
track.label: Pick a track cell in the Rails group. The Cell section toggles its six segments and picks the open segment of its switch; Shift+R turns the tracks a quarter turn. Something enters only through a side a segment opens and leaves along a segment that joins its entry side.

ports.name: Gate ports
ports.label: A data latch takes data and clock links, a counter takes count up and count down links. The Connections rows name each link's role and Swap inputs or Swap outputs exchanges them. The validator warns about a data latch with no clock or data.

chain.name: Chain push
chain.label: Nothing to place: an ice block pushes ice and arrow blocks, an arrow block pushes dirt, ice and arrow blocks, so a line moves in one push. A wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

canopy.name: Canopy
canopy.label: Use the Canopy brush in the Terrain tab: click toggles a cell, a drag repeats the first cell's choice, the eraser clears it, and thin walls are kept. It stops bugs and rovers.

players.name: Several players
players.label: Use the Second Player tool to place up to 7 more starts; pick each one's character or remove it in the Cell section, and turn it with R or Shift+R. One player is controlled at a time and V swaps to the next; each keeps its own keys and tools, chips are shared, and every player must reach an exit.

trap.name: Trap control and trap
trap.label: A trap control opens the next trap after it in reading order, or the first trap when none follows. A trap is open while any control that works it is pressed; a trap no control works stays closed.

teleport.name: Red and blue teleports
teleport.label: A teleport sends to the previous teleport of its colour in reading order, and the first one sends to the last. A teleport that is occupied, or whose exits are blocked, is skipped for the one before it; a lone teleport goes nowhere.

clone.name: Clone switch, machine and template
clone.label: A clone switch works the nearest clone machine (on a tie, the first in reading order). The creature or block standing on a machine is its template. When the switch is pressed, the template leaves the way the machine faces, or its own facing on a machine with no direction, and a copy takes its place. If its way out is blocked, nothing happens.

laser.name: Laser controller and shooter
laser.label: A laser controller fires the nearest laser shooter (on a tie, the first in reading order) once each time something that works switches steps onto it. With no shooter it fires nothing.

toggle.name: Toggle control and door
toggle.label: Each time something that works switches steps onto a toggle control, every toggle door of its colour flips between open and closed; leaving changes nothing. A control with no door of its colour flips nothing.

hold.name: Plate and hold door
hold.label: A hold door of a colour is open only while every plate of its colour is pressed. A colour with no plates keeps its doors closed.

golem_blue.name: Blue golem control and golems
golem_blue.label: Each time something that works switches starts a step onto a blue golem control, every blue golem turns around.

golem_yellow.name: Yellow golem control and golems
golem_yellow.label: Each time the player steps onto a yellow golem control, every yellow golem tries to take one step in the direction the player was moving. Only the player works it.

top_layer.label: Toggle controls, clone switches, laser controllers, golem controls and teleports work only from the top layer of their cell; plates and trap controls work from any layer.

how.label: Link each brown button to its traps (K or Link...).

unlinked.label: With no link, a trap stays open while any brown button is held.

how.label: Link each red button to its clone machines (K or Link...).

unlinked.label: With no link, a red button fires every clone machine holding a monster or block.

how.label: Link each shot trigger to its launchers (K or Link...).

unlinked.label: A shot trigger fires only its linked launchers: with no link it fires nothing.

how.label: Link each signal plate, signal button, laser receiver or gate to the gates, hold doors, shot launchers and clone machines it feeds (K or Link...). Cycles are refused. A launcher or clone machine fires once each time its signal starts.

unlinked.label: A gate with no signal linked into it stays off. A hold door with none follows its pressure plates of the same colour. A launcher or clone machine fired by no signal only answers its buttons.

how.label: A hold door and its pressure plates share a colour.

unlinked.label: A hold door is open while every plate of its colour is pressed; with no plate it is shut.

how.label: A toggle button flips the toggle walls of its colour (the plain green button flips the plain toggle walls).

unlinked.label: A toggle wall with no button of its colour never flips.

how.label: Teleporters of one colour form a group; each sends to the previous one of its group in reading order.

unlinked.label: A teleporter alone in its group goes nowhere.

how.label: A laser gate is open while a beam lights any laser receiver of its group (same colour).

unlinked.label: A receiver with no gate of its group opens nothing, and a gate with no receiver stays shut.

how.label: Blue buttons turn every tank around; no link needed, the whole level answers.

unlinked.label: With no blue button, tanks never turn around.

how.label: Orange buttons toggle flame jets; no link needed, the whole level answers.

unlinked.label: With no orange button, flame jets are never toggled.

how.label: A gray button swaps the chips and bombs within radius {radius} of it.

unlinked.label: With nothing within reach, a gray button swaps nothing.

how.label: Puppet controls steer every puppet in the level.

unlinked.label: With no puppet control, puppets do not step with the player.

stacked_terrain.label: Epoxy plays this element as CC3D does.

gravel.name: Gravel
gravel.label: Epoxy plays plain gravel as CC3D does: the player and every block may enter it, monsters may not.

gravel_with_reflector.name: Gravel in a level with a reflector
gravel_with_reflector.label: Epoxy gravel admits mirrors, where CC3D gravel refuses reflectors.

socket_red_stacked.name: Red socket over another layer
socket_red_stacked.label: CC3D plans a red socket against the layer below it, which Epoxy does not do.

orb_speed.name: Speed orb
orb_speed.label: Epoxy slow-time boots slow the monsters only, where the CC3D speed orb also slows the blocks monsters push.

water.name: Water
water.label: A dirt block makes dirt, an ice block ice and a colour block a bridge, as in CC3D. The Epoxy walker and golems walk into water and drown, where the CC3D ones refuse it, and Epoxy lets a second block be pushed onto a floating colour block.

force_random.name: Random force floor
force_random.label: Epoxy draws the direction at random instead of a fixed cycle.

socket.name: Blue socket
socket.label: Epoxy plays the blue socket as its fish gate: shut while a chip is left, then open to the player, a block or a monster, and the first to enter turns it into floor, as in CC3D.

slime.name: Slime
slime.label: Slime kills the player and is cleaned by any block that enters it, as in CC3D. With the fire and the water orb together CC3D lets the player through, where Epoxy kills him; and a CC3D walker or golem refuses slime, where the Epoxy one dies in it.

turtle.name: Turtle
turtle.label: The turtle sinks behind whoever leaves it, as in CC3D. The Epoxy walker and golems refuse a turtle, where the CC3D ones cross it and sink it.

dirt.name: Dirt
dirt.label: The player clears dirt by walking into it, as in CC3D. Epoxy refuses a block on dirt, where CC3D lets a block clear it.

teleport_blue.name: Blue teleport
teleport_blue.label: Epoxy plays the blue teleporter as its forward teleporter: the target is the previous blue teleporter in reading order, and the exit of the player, a block or a monster is forward only, as in CC3D.

teleport_red.name: Red teleport
teleport_red.label: Epoxy plays the red teleporter as its turning teleporter: the target is the previous red teleporter in reading order, and the exit of the player, a block or a monster is forward, then right, then left, then back, as in CC3D.

appearing_wall.name: Appearing wall
appearing_wall.label: The player bumping an appearing wall makes a wall, as in CC3D. A pushed block or a monster also makes a wall in CC3D, where Epoxy leaves it as it is.

trap.name: Trap
trap.label: Epoxy plays the trap as CC3D does: it holds what enters it until a control works it, and each control works the next trap after it in reading order.

trap_control.name: Trap control
trap_control.label: Epoxy plays the trap control as CC3D does: it works the next trap after it in reading order.

clone_machine.name: Clone machine
clone_machine.label: Epoxy plays the clone machine as CC3D does for a block or a golem as template. Other monster templates keep the approximation of their monster.

clone_switch.name: Clone switch
clone_switch.label: Epoxy plays the clone switch as CC3D does: it works the nearest machine, whether the player or a block steps onto it.

golem_control_blue.name: Blue golem control
golem_control_blue.label: Epoxy plays the blue golem control as CC3D does: every golem turns round when the player, a block or a golem steps onto it.

bomb.name: Bomb
bomb.label: Epoxy plays the bomb as CC3D does: it kills the player who steps on it and is spent with any block or monster that enters it.

gate_tools.name: Tool gate
gate_tools.label: The gate takes every tool of the player who enters it, as in CC3D. Epoxy refuses the ice block, which CC3D slides over the gate.

gate_keys.name: Key gate
gate_keys.label: The gate takes every key of the player who enters it, as in CC3D. Epoxy refuses the ice block, which CC3D slides over the gate.

orb_ice.name: Ice orb
orb_ice.label: The orb works as in CC3D. CC3D holds at most four tools and a fifth drops the oldest on the cell, where Epoxy keeps every pair of boots.

orb_force.name: Force orb
orb_force.label: The orb works as in CC3D. CC3D holds at most four tools and a fifth drops the oldest on the cell, where Epoxy keeps every pair of boots.

orb_fire.name: Fire orb
orb_fire.label: The orb works as in CC3D. CC3D holds at most four tools and a fifth drops the oldest on the cell, where Epoxy keeps every pair of boots. With the fire and the water orb together CC3D lets the player cross slime and cleans it, where Epoxy kills him.

orb_water.name: Water orb
orb_water.label: The orb works as in CC3D. CC3D holds at most four tools and a fifth drops the oldest on the cell, where Epoxy keeps every pair of boots. With the fire and the water orb together CC3D lets the player cross slime and cleans it, where Epoxy kills him.

block_dirt.name: Dirt block
block_dirt.label: Plates, slime, bombs, ice and force floors behave as in CC3D. Epoxy lets the block into fire and onto an item, which CC3D refuses, and refuses dirt and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block clear.

block_ice.name: Ice block
block_ice.label: Fire, water, slime, bombs, ice and plates behave as in CC3D. Epoxy refuses dirt, a chain of blocks, the security gates and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block slide over or clear.

plate_red.name: Pressure plate (red)
plate_red.label: Plates and hold doors agree with CC3D for the player and every block, and monsters press them as in CC3D, the blinky and the screamer excepted, which press nothing in either.

plate_green.name: Pressure plate (green)
plate_green.label: Plates and hold doors agree with CC3D for the player and every block, and monsters press them as in CC3D, the blinky and the screamer excepted, which press nothing in either.

plate_blue.name: Pressure plate (blue)
plate_blue.label: Plates and hold doors agree with CC3D for the player and every block, and monsters press them as in CC3D, the blinky and the screamer excepted, which press nothing in either.

plate_yellow.name: Pressure plate (yellow)
plate_yellow.label: Plates and hold doors agree with CC3D for the player and every block, and monsters press them as in CC3D, the blinky and the screamer excepted, which press nothing in either.

block_color_red.name: Colour block (red)
block_color_red.label: Plates, slime, bombs, ice and force floors behave as in CC3D. Epoxy lets the block into fire and onto an item, which CC3D refuses, and refuses dirt and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block clear.

block_color_green.name: Colour block (green)
block_color_green.label: Plates, slime, bombs, ice and force floors behave as in CC3D. Epoxy lets the block into fire and onto an item, which CC3D refuses, and refuses dirt and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block clear.

block_color_blue.name: Colour block (blue)
block_color_blue.label: Plates, slime, bombs, ice and force floors behave as in CC3D. Epoxy lets the block into fire and onto an item, which CC3D refuses, and refuses dirt and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block clear.

block_color_yellow.name: Colour block (yellow)
block_color_yellow.label: Plates, slime, bombs, ice and force floors behave as in CC3D. Epoxy lets the block into fire and onto an item, which CC3D refuses, and refuses dirt and an open blue gate, which CC3D lets the block clear.

reflector.name: Reflector
reflector.label: Epoxy plays a reflector as a one-sided mirror: it turns shots and beams from its two reflecting faces and destroys a shot coming from behind. Mirrors are turned to match their reflecting faces. Bounce timing differs from CC3D.

walker.name: Walker
walker.label: Epoxy plays the walker as a monster of its own: straight on, one random draw when blocked, a four-tick step, refusing water, fire and slime. Its random draws cannot be matched step by step with CC3D.

legs_green.name: Green legs
legs_green.label: Epoxy plays the green legs as a monster of their own, with the CC3D turn order (straight, right, left, back) and pace. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D. The real game switches the legs' pattern with the plates; neither CC3D nor Epoxy reproduces it.

legs_red.name: Red legs
legs_red.label: Epoxy plays the red legs as a monster of their own, with the CC3D turn order (straight, left, right, back) and pace. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D. The real game switches the legs' pattern with the plates; neither CC3D nor Epoxy reproduces it.

blinky.name: Blinky
blinky.label: Epoxy plays the blinky as a monster of its own: same turn order and pace, immune to water, not carried by ice or force floors, crossing turtles without sinking them, pressing no plate. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

baby_blinky.name: Baby blinky
baby_blinky.label: Epoxy plays the baby blinky as a monster of its own: same turn order and pace, immune to water only, crossing turtles without sinking them, pressing plates. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

limpa.name: Limpa
limpa.label: Epoxy plays the limpa as a monster of its own: same turn order and pace as in CC3D, refusing water, fire and slime. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

limpy.name: Limpy
limpy.label: Epoxy plays the limpy as a monster of its own: same turn order and pace as in CC3D, refusing water, fire and slime. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

bouncer.name: Bouncer
bouncer.label: Epoxy plays the bouncer as a monster of its own: same path and pace as in CC3D, refusing water, fire and slime. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

omni.name: Omni
omni.label: Epoxy plays the omni as a monster of its own: one random draw per step, a wait when blocked, an eight-tick step, immune to slime, leaving slime behind once it has stood on slime. Its random draws cannot be matched step by step with CC3D.

screamer.name: Screamer
screamer.label: Epoxy plays the screamer as a monster of its own: immune to fire, not carried by ice or force floors, melting the ice blocks in its way, pressing no plate. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

baby_screamer.name: Baby screamer
baby_screamer.label: Epoxy plays the baby screamer as a monster of its own: immune to fire only, melting the ice blocks in its way, pressing plates. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

snappy.name: Snappy
snappy.label: Epoxy plays the snappy as a monster of its own: it chases along the axis of the greater distance, with its rest folded into an eight-tick step. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

bot_static.name: Static bot
bot_static.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_cw.name: Clockwise bot
bot_cw.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_ccw.name: Counter-clockwise bot
bot_ccw.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

bot_multi.name: Multi-turn bot
bot_multi.label: Epoxy plays a bot as a turret: the beam and its turn period are close to CC3D, with a beam length and a period that are guesses, and Epoxy makes no turn at the first step.

golem_yellow.name: Yellow golem
golem_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the yellow golem as a monster of its own, steered by the puppet control, with the path, the stops and the pushes of CC3D. A CC3D golem walks its cell in four ticks, from a tick after the player settles, where the Epoxy one steps at once, and a CC3D golem makes an appearing wall a wall where Epoxy leaves it. The blocks it pushes carry the gaps of the Epoxy blocks.

golem_control_yellow.name: Yellow golem control
golem_control_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the yellow golem control as the puppet control: only the player works it, and a golem or block entering it does nothing, as in CC3D. It also steers the Epoxy puppets.

nibble.name: Nibble
nibble.label: Epoxy plays the nibble as a monster of its own: it runs away along the axis of the greater distance, with its rest folded into an eight-tick step. Entering ice or a force floor is a normal step in Epoxy and a fast one in CC3D, and a monster that reaches the player stands on his cell in Epoxy and next to him in CC3D.

golem_blue.name: Blue golem
golem_blue.label: The path, the stops and the turn at the control match CC3D. A CC3D golem is faster (4 ticks per cell against 6), stops before water and slime where an Epoxy golem is lost, enters an open blue gate, and stops next to the player instead of stepping onto him.

laser_controller.name: Laser controller
laser_controller.label: Epoxy plays the laser controller as a shot trigger linked to the shooters it fires (CC3D uses the nearest shooter). In CC3D any monster works it; in Epoxy anything that steps on it does. A trigger hidden under a removable top acts only once revealed.

laser_shooter.name: Laser shooter
laser_shooter.label: Epoxy plays the shooter as a shot launcher: a wall-like tile that fires the way it faces, so the terrain under the shooter is flattened. A shot crosses cells at the CC3D pace, but its opacity follows Epoxy laser transparency, and the exit and the first cell hit can differ.

trap_unworked.name: Trap without a control
trap_unworked.label: No trap control works this trap: CC3D keeps it shut, where Epoxy opens an unlinked trap with any brown button. An Epoxy trap link has no empty form, so the converter cannot keep it shut.

clone_switch_empty.name: Clone switch with nothing to clone
clone_switch_empty.label: The nearest clone machine of this switch holds no template Epoxy can clone (none, or a laser shooter): CC3D does nothing, and a switch left unlinked would fire every machine in Epoxy, so the converter drops the switch link.

bomb_with_item.name: Bomb sharing a cell with an item
bomb_with_item.label: A bomb layer shares its cell with an item: Epoxy holds one item per cell, so the bomb is dropped and the item stays.

laser_shooter_covered.name: Laser shooter on an item or another layer
laser_shooter_covered.label: The shooter stands on an item or on a layer other than plain floor (a device, a machine, ground): the Epoxy launcher replaces the whole cell, so what was there is dropped, and a shooter used as a clone template is not cloned.

stacked_runtime.name: Stack that acts while covered
stacked_runtime.label: The stack has a layer that acts while covered under a top that is not a door or a socket, or more layers than a removable top and the one it hides, which Epoxy flattens.

hold_door_red.name: Hold door (red)
hold_door_red.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_green.name: Hold door (green)
hold_door_green.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_blue.name: Hold door (blue)
hold_door_blue.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

hold_door_yellow.name: Hold door (yellow)
hold_door_yellow.label: Epoxy plays the hold door as CC3D does: all plates of its colour, occupant may leave, nobody may enter.

Blocks entering through its south and east sides. Leaving through a blocked side pushes it round a quarter turn (as in Chip's Challenge 2); leaving through an open side leaves it as it is.
Blocks entering through its south and west sides. Leaving through a blocked side pushes it round a quarter turn (as in Chip's Challenge 2); leaving through an open side leaves it as it is.
Blocks entering through its north and west sides. Leaving through a blocked side pushes it round a quarter turn (as in Chip's Challenge 2); leaving through an open side leaves it as it is.
Open on its north and south sides, closed on the other two. Walkers, sliders, blocks and teleport exits only get in or out through an open side. Beams and shots pass over it.
Open on its east and west sides, closed on the other two. Walkers, sliders, blocks and teleport exits only get in or out through an open side. Beams and shots pass over it.
Open on its north and east sides, closed on the other two. A monster that comes in follows the curve and leaves by the other open side. Beams and shots pass over it.

Open on its north and west sides, closed on the other two. A monster that comes in follows the curve and leaves by the other open side. Beams and shots pass over it.
A bent rail open on its south and east sides that swaps with its twin, open on south and west, each time a green button is pressed. Needs: a green button.

Swaps a monster that arrives on it for its paired kind (bug and paramecium, glider and fireball, teeth and skitter, pink ball and walker). The player who steps on it switches between Chip and Melinda.

Turns an arrow block that arrives on it a quarter turn counter-clockwise, arrows included. Only arrow blocks turn: monsters and the player are not affected.
Pushes east, then south, west and north in turn. The turn is shared by the whole level: every arrival of the player, a block or a monster on any such floor takes the next direction.

Pick it up, then drop it where you want. It lights when you step off its cell and blasts about four seconds later. The blast covers a 5 by 5 square without its four far corners: it destroys every item, kills every monster, block and you, and turns walls, doors, water and other terrain into floor. Steel walls, sockets and logic gates resist.
Blasts a few seconds after you left it. Another blast destroys it before it goes off. It blocks nothing and cannot be picked up.

Pick it up, then set it down on plain floor where you want. The pads you set down link with each other: step onto one and you come out of another. A single pad does nothing, and a pad stays where it is.
A pad set down from a Pocket Gate. It links with the other Pocket Gate pads of the level, in reverse reading order. Blocks and monsters use it too. It cannot be picked up again.

A relay pad that is switched off: plain floor. Link a signal to it and it lights while the signal is on. Lit relay pads send you to the previous lit relay pad in reading order. Without a link it stays as placed.
A relay pad that is switched on: a teleporter that links only with the other lit relay pads. Link a signal to it and it goes dark while the signal is off. Without a link it stays as placed.

Pick it up and keep it. The first time you step on a thief that would take your boots or your keys, the token is spent instead and nothing is taken. A thief with nothing to take leaves it alone. It cannot be set down, and a thief never takes it.

Pick it up, then throw it at what is in front of you. It flies until it hits something: it kills a monster, sets off a bomb and melts an ice block, and a mirror turns it. It is used up where it stops, and it kills you if a mirror sends it back.
Counts as a chip. Every press of a green button turns it into a green bomb, and back.
Explodes like a bomb. Every press of a green button turns it into a green chip, and back.
Let Melinda walk on dirt and gravel. They do nothing for Chip.
While the player holds it, the wire floor they stand on sends a signal along its wires.
Pick it up and keep it. Bumping into a plain wall turns that wall into a steel wall; you do not move and the foil is not used up. A thief takes it with the other boots.
Stays where it is. Stepping on it pauses the level timer, and stepping on it again resumes it. Monsters and blocks cannot enter its cell. It does nothing on a level without a time limit.
Pick it up and keep it. Each time you step on a thief, one bribe is spent and nothing is taken, whether it guards boots or keys. It cannot be set down, and a thief never takes it.

A Chip's Challenge 2 track cell with up to six track segments. You may only come in through a side a track opens, and you leave only along a track that joins the side you came in by; a blocked step is turned onto the track. A cell with a switch uses one track at a time and moves to the next when something leaves along the active track. Blocks may back out. The railroad sign ignores the tracks.
Pick it up and keep it. While you hold it, track cells no longer limit where you come in or out. A thief takes it with the other boots.
While held, every monster takes twice as long per step. A thief takes it.
Flips every plain toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: toggle walls (not the coloured ones, which have their own toggle buttons).
Makes every tank turn round. Needs: tanks.
Opens traps while held. Link it to traps with K or Link...; a trap that no link names opens with any brown button.
A spot to cover with a block. Needs: the win rule that asks to cover every target.
Fires clone machines. Link it to machines with K or Link...; with no link, it fires every clone machine that holds a creature.
Turns every flame jet on or off. Needs: flame jets.
Swaps the chips and bombs within two cells of it (a 5 x 5 area).
Harmless while off. An orange button turns it on. Needs: an orange button.
Burns the player unless they wear fire boots; only fire-proof monsters enter it, and lighting it kills monsters on it and melts ice blocks. An orange button turns it off. Needs: an orange button.
A wall until a green button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a green button.
Open floor until a green button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a green button.
Sends whatever enters it to the previous plain teleporter in reading order, wrapping round; it skips ones whose exit is blocked. Needs: a second teleporter.
Chains only with red teleporters. Needs: another red teleporter.
Chains only with blue teleporters. Needs: another blue teleporter.
Shut while a chip is left. Once the last chip is in, the player, a block or a monster may enter it, and the first to do so turns it into floor. Needs: chips to collect.
Chains only with other forward teleporters, and sends the player, a block or a monster out of the previous one in reading order, straight ahead only. Needs: another forward teleporter.

Chains only with other turning teleporters, and sends the player, a block or a monster out of the previous one in reading order: straight ahead, else to the right, else to the left, else back. Needs: another turning teleporter.
Kills the player and most monsters. A dirt block or an ice block clears it and survives; any other block is destroyed as it cleans the slime.
The player, blocks and monsters may step on it, except fireballs and ghosts. It sinks into water behind whatever leaves it; a glider leaves it afloat.
Lights each time the signal wired into it changes. The orange button does not touch it. Needs: a signal link into it.

Burns the player unless they wear fire boots, and any monster that is not fire-proof while it stands in it; monsters may still walk in. It goes out each time the signal wired into it changes. The orange button does not touch it. Needs: a signal link into it.
The player and monsters walk over it, but no block may enter it. It never changes.

Swaps a monster or a block that arrives on it by the Chip's Challenge 2 table: bug into glider, glider into paramecium, paramecium into fireball, fireball into bug; pink ball and walker; teeth and timid teeth; dirt block and ice block. A blob becomes a monster drawn by chance from glider, paramecium, fireball, bug, walker, pink ball, teeth, tank and timid teeth (the same draw at every replay). Anything else, items included, passes unchanged.
Chains only with other random teleporters, and sends the player, a block or a monster out of one of the others, picked by chance (the same pick at every replay). Needs: another random teleporter.
Chains only with other CC2 red teleporters, and sends the player, a block or a monster out of one of them by the Chip's Challenge 2 exit order. Needs: another CC2 red teleporter.
While the player holds it, touching a monster or a block does the player no harm.

The player clears it by walking in; monsters cannot enter. A dirt block, a colour block or an ice block may enter. A dirt block or a colour block turns it into floor; an ice block passes over and leaves it.

The player may step on it; among the monsters only rovers and ghosts may enter; every block but a dirt block may enter. It turns into a wall behind whatever leaves it, unless another actor still stands on it.
A trap that starts open and holds nothing. The first time a linked button or wire releases or loses power, it becomes an ordinary trap. Needs: a link from a button or a signal source.
Looks like floor. It turns into a wall when the player bumps into it, when a pushed block hits it or when a monster tries to enter it.
Kills the player and most monsters. A player holding both fire boots and water boots survives and turns the cell into floor. A block is destroyed as it cleans the slime.
The unpowered form of the CC2 red teleporter: it is not a teleporter, so nothing is sent to it and nothing leaves by it. Needs: a signal link into it.
The unpowered form of the CC2 transmogrifier: whatever arrives on it passes unchanged. Needs: a signal link into it.
Chains only with yellow teleporters. Needs: another yellow teleporter.
Chains only with green teleporters. Needs: another green teleporter.
Holds whatever steps in until a brown button is held. Needs: a brown button (link it with K or Link...; a trap that no link names stays open while any brown button is held down).
Copies the monster or block on it, turrets included, into the cell it faces when its red button is pressed. Needs: a red button, and a creature on the machine.
Casts a straight beam to the north that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the east that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the south that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Casts a straight beam to the west that kills the player and monsters. Mirrors turn it 90 degrees; walls stop it.
Holds the red laser gates open while a beam lights it. Needs: a laser emitter, and red laser gates.
Holds the blue laser gates open while a beam lights it. Needs: a laser emitter, and blue laser gates.
Open while a red laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a red laser receiver.
Open while a red laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a red laser receiver.
Open while a blue laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a blue laser receiver.
Open while a blue laser receiver is lit, closed otherwise. Needs: a blue laser receiver.
A red hold door stays open while every red plate is pressed. Needs: a red hold door.
A green hold door stays open while every green plate is pressed. Needs: a green hold door.
A blue hold door stays open while every blue plate is pressed. Needs: a blue hold door.
A yellow hold door stays open while every yellow plate is pressed. Needs: a yellow hold door.
Sends a signal while something stands on it. Needs: a signal link to a gate or a hold door.
Sends a signal for one moment each time something steps on it. Needs: a signal link to a gate, a hold door, a shot launcher or a clone machine.
Sends a signal while every linked input is sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Sends a signal while any linked input is sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Sends a signal while its one linked input is not sending one. Needs: one signal link in, and one out.
Sends a signal while an odd number of its linked inputs are sending one. Needs: signal links in and out.
Flips between sending and not sending each time its input starts sending; starts off. Needs: signal links in and out.
Flips between sending and not sending each time its input starts sending; starts on. Needs: signal links in and out.
Sends a signal unless every signal linked into it is sending. Needs: signal links in and out.
Remembers the signal on its data link (port in0) while its clock link (port in1) is sending, and sends what it remembers. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 0. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 1. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 2. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 3. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 4. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 5. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 6. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 7. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 8. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.

Counts up on each start of its first input (in0) and down on each start of its second (in1), from 0 to 9; starts at 9. Wrapping past 9 sends a short pulse on out0; wrapping below 0 sends on out1 until the next count. Needs: signal links in and out.
A floor a wire runs under. It sends a signal while the player stands on it holding the lightning bolt. Needs: signal links out.
A wall that becomes a purple floor each time the signal wired into it changes, whether it starts or stops sending. Needs: a signal link into it.
A floor that becomes a purple wall each time the signal wired into it changes, whether it starts or stops sending. Needs: a signal link into it.
Sends no signal. Each time something steps on it, it turns on. Needs: a signal link to a gate or a device.
Sends a signal. Each time something steps on it, it turns off. Needs: a signal link to a gate or a device.
Sends a signal all the time, except while something stands on it. Needs: a signal link to a gate or a device.

Each time something steps on it, it pulses every wired device within two cells (a 5 x 5 area), with no wire from the button: flip tiles flip, launchers and clone machines fire once, and hold doors, relay pads and wired traps open for one moment.
Holds whatever steps in, and opens while the signal wired into it is on or while a brown button is held. Needs: a signal link into it.
Harmless while off. It lights each time the signal wired into it changes. The orange button does not touch it. Needs: a signal link into it.

Burns the player unless they wear fire boots; only fire-proof monsters enter it. It goes out each time the signal wired into it changes. The orange button does not touch it. Needs: a signal link into it.
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a red pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a red pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a green pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a green pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a blue pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a blue pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Opens while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a yellow pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
Open while something stands on every pressure plate of its colour. Needs: a yellow pressure plate (without one it stays shut).
A wall until a red toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a red toggle button.
Open floor until a red toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a red toggle button.
A wall until a blue toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a blue toggle button.
Open floor until a blue toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a blue toggle button.
A wall until a yellow toggle button is pressed, then it opens. Needs: a yellow toggle button.
Open floor until a yellow toggle button is pressed, then it closes. Needs: a yellow toggle button.
Flips every red toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: red toggle walls.
Flips every blue toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: blue toggle walls.
Flips every yellow toggle wall between closed and open. Needs: yellow toggle walls.
When the player ends a move on it, every puppet steps one cell the same way the player moved, pushing a block if one is in the way. Needs: puppets.

Fires a shot to the north when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the east when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the south when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...

Fires a shot to the west when a shot trigger linked to it is pressed. A shot kills the player, monsters and turrets, melts ice blocks, sets off bombs and turns off mirrors; walls, other blocks and items stop it. Needs: a shot trigger linked with K or Link...
Fires its linked launchers. Needs: launchers linked with K or Link... (unlinked, it fires nothing).
Walkable, like floor. It is what a red colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a green colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a blue colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
Walkable, like floor. It is what a yellow colour block becomes when it is pushed into water.
A wall driven by CC2 wires. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
The wire-driven floor paired with the CC2 purple wall. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A switch worked by stepping on it. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A wire button of CC2. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A wire gate that counts pulses. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A wire logic gate. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
The CC2 gray button, which is not the Epoxy one. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A junction piece of the CC2 tracks. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
An orange button that acts on its neighbours only. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A wall that resists blasts. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A tile code the importer does not know. Epoxy does not play it: it acts as a wall.
A CC2 item. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A chip that the green button flips. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A bomb that the green button flips. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 bomb that blasts after a delay. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 item. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 item. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 item. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 item that stops or starts the clock. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A chip that does not count toward the required total. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
CC2 boots. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 sign. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A CC2 sign. Epoxy does not play it: it does nothing.
A block the player can push. Pushed into water, it turns the water into dirt.

A pushable block that moves only toward the one side that shows an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

A pushable block that moves only toward the two opposite sides that show an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

A pushable block that moves only toward the two adjacent sides that show an arrow. Pushed from any other side, it stays still. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

A pushable block that moves only toward the three sides that show an arrow. Pushed from the fourth side, it stays still. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

A pushable block that moves toward all four sides, each of which shows an arrow. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.

A pushable block that slides on ice and force floors, turns water into ice and melts into water in fire. A push also moves the dirt blocks, ice blocks, colour blocks and arrow blocks lined up ahead of it; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push. It slides over security gates without opening them, and it passes over CC3D dirt without clearing it.
A block with no arrow: no push moves it, whether from the player, a monster or another block. It still slides when it rides ice or a force floor.

A block the player can push. Turns water into ice when pushed into it, and melts into water in fire; a shot also destroys it, leaving water only on plain floor. Pushed, it moves a line of ice blocks and arrow blocks along with it, never a dirt block; a wall, the map edge or a sliding block ahead refuses the whole push.
A creature that does not move on its own: it steps only when the player works a puppet control. It presses plates and pushes blocks. Needs: a puppet control.

Hides in the floor and does not move. It wakes when you arrive on (or slide through) a cell next to it, not diagonally, and after a short pause chases you slowly for good. Touching it while it sleeps is deadly.
Chases the player at a slow pace. It never goes back to sleep.

Drifts straight ahead through walls, doors, water, fire, ice and force floors alike; terrain has no effect on it and it presses no plate. Only a thin wall, the map edge or any other entity (a monster, a block, a mirror, a turret) stops it: it then turns round once, and stays put if it is blocked both ways. It kills on contact. A shot, a laser beam, a thrown stone, a blast or a ward destroys it. It cannot be cloned.
Chases the player like teeth, but four times slower, and is drawn almost like plain floor (only a faint mark shows it in the editor). It kills on contact.
Teeth in reverse: runs away from Chip and chases Melinda. Ordinary teeth chase Chip and run away from Melinda. It kills on contact.

Goes straight on, else turns left, right or back. It walks through walls, doors, sockets and thin walls, but not through steel walls, clone machines or water. Ice, force floors, rails, traps, bombs, fire and slime do not affect it; it walks over items without picking them up and works the buttons it crosses. It kills on contact.
Moves like teeth, glider, bug, pink ball, timid teeth, fireball, paramecium and walker in turn, changing after 32 steps decided. It kills on contact.
Goes straight on and turns back when blocked. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Chases the player along the axis where the distance is greater, trying the other axis only when it is not lined up with the player, and rests a step after each step. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Runs away from the player along the axis where the distance is greater, trying the other axis only when it is not lined up with the player, and rests a step after each step. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Goes straight on, else turns left, right or back. Water does not stop it, ice and force floors do not carry it, and it crosses turtles without sinking them. It presses no plate and works no switch. It will not step into fire or slime. It kills on contact.

Goes straight on, else turns left, right or back. Water does not stop it and it crosses turtles without sinking them, but ice and force floors carry it. It works plates and switches. It will not step into fire or slime. It kills on contact.
Prefers to turn right, else goes straight on, else left, else back, so it follows the wall on its right. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.
Prefers to turn left, else goes straight on, else right, else back, so it follows the wall on its left. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Moves slowly: it draws a direction at random and waits when that way is blocked. Slime does not hurt it, and once it has stood on slime it leaves slime on the bare floor it steps out of. It will not step into water or fire. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.
Goes straight on, else turns right, left or back. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.
Goes straight on, else turns left, right or back. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Goes straight on, else turns right, left or back. Fire does not stop it and ice and force floors do not carry it. It melts the ice block in its way, and the floor under the block becomes water. It presses no plate and works no switch. It will not step into water or slime. It kills on contact.

Goes straight on, else turns right, left or back. Fire does not stop it, and it melts the ice block in its way (the floor under the block becomes water), but ice and force floors carry it. It works plates and switches. It will not step into water or slime. It kills on contact.

Goes straight on; when blocked it draws a direction at random and waits if that way is blocked too. It steps in four ticks. It will not step into water, fire or slime. It works plates and switches and kills on contact.

Walks straight on and stops at a wall or anything that blocks a monster; it does not turn by itself. A blue button turns it round, and it turns round itself when it steps onto one. It steps in four ticks, is carried by ice and force floors, works plates and switches, and will not step into water, fire or slime. It kills on contact.

Does not move on its own: it takes one step in the direction the player was moving each time the player steps onto a puppet control. It pushes one block, presses plates and switches, is not carried by ice or force floors, walks over sand and turtles, and is lost in water, fire and slime. It kills on contact. Needs: a puppet control.

Copies every move Chip tries to make, even a blocked one, and does nothing while Melinda is the player. It follows Chip's rules: it opens green doors without using the key, slides on ice, pushes blocks, takes keys and boots on its way, presses buttons, and dies in water, fire and bombs (the level goes on). Touching it kills the player, whoever moves into the other.

Copies every move Melinda tries to make, even a blocked one, and does nothing while Chip is the player. It follows Melinda's rules: it opens yellow doors without using the key, does not slide on ice, is stopped by dirt and gravel, pushes blocks, takes keys and boots on its way, presses buttons, and dies in water, fire and bombs (the level goes on). Touching it kills the player, whoever moves into the other.
Runs from the player, first along the axis where it is farther away (sideways on a tie), then the other; when lined up it backs straight away.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam in the way it faces, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It never turns.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It turns clockwise every 60 ticks.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam, killing the first player or monster it reaches. It turns counter-clockwise every 60 ticks.
A pushable block that fires a 3-cell beam on all four sides, killing the first player or monster each beam reaches.
A pushable mirror that turns a laser beam or a shot 90 degrees. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a laser beam or a shot 90 degrees. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its north-east face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its north-west face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its south-east face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable mirror that turns a beam or a shot only on its south-west face; a shot from behind destroys it; a laser beam from behind just stops on it. It refuses water.
A pushable block that presses only the red pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.
A pushable block that presses only the green pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.

A pushable block that presses only the yellow pressure plates (other blocks and the player press any). Pushed into water, it floats as a walkable block.
The second player of CC2. Epoxy has one player: she stays where she is and does nothing.
A player that copies the moves of the first one. Epoxy does not play it: it stays where it is.
A second player that copies the moves of the first one. Epoxy does not play it: it stays where it is.

A CC2 monster. Epoxy does not play it: it stays where it is.

level_1.title: Power Up
level_1.hint: Collect every chip to open the socket, then step through the exit.

level_2.title: Color Codes
level_2.hint: A key opens the door of its color and is used up. Green keys stay in your pocket.

level_3.title: Landfill
level_3.hint: Push a block into water to make dirt you can walk over. Blocks cannot cross dirt, so walk on it first. The wide channel needs two blocks in the same row.

level_4.title: Dress Code
level_4.hint: Flippers carry you across water, fire boots through flames. Find them in the right order.

level_5.title: Black Ice
level_5.hint: On ice you slide until you reach solid ground. Curved corners turn your slide.

level_6.title: One Way Ticket
level_6.hint: Conveyors only run one way. Force boots let you walk against them.

level_7.title: Airlock
level_7.hint: A green button flips every toggle wall. A wall that closes behind you opens again at the next press.

level_8.title: Hold the Line
level_8.hint: A trap holds whatever enters it while its brown button is free. Park a block on the button first.

level_9.title: Blast Radius
level_9.hint: A block pushed into a bomb destroys both. Count the bombs before you spend a block: one is needed for the water.

level_10.title: Relay
level_10.hint: A pad sends you to the pad of the same color, still moving the same way. The side you enter from decides where you land.

level_11.title: Allotments
level_11.hint: Thin fences stop you and blocks on one edge only. Blocks cannot cross dirt: walk on it first to clear the way.

level_12.title: Workshop
level_12.hint: Every wing holds a key or a chip. The conveyor out of the east wing runs one way, and the green button where it ends opens the way back.

level_13.title: Night Shift
level_13.hint: Bugs keep a wall on their left and never step on gravel or on an item. Wait in a gravel nook, then move when the way is clear.

level_14.title: Ricochet
level_14.hint: Balls roll straight and bounce back off anything, chips included. Take a chip and its lane grows longer.

level_15.title: Reverse Gear
level_15.hint: Tanks drive straight until something stops them. The blue button turns every tank around: stand clear of their tracks when you press it, and never wait in the bay at the bottom.

level_16.title: Mirage
level_16.hint: Some blue walls melt when you walk into them, others hold. Below, invisible walls appear only when you bump into them.

level_17.title: Assembly Line
level_17.hint: Each press of the red button makes a new block in the machine. Blocks are free: if one gets stuck, make another.

level_18.title: Dash
level_18.hint: Teeth chase you but move slower than you. The clock is tight: plan your loop around the pillars before you start.

level_19.title: Pickpocket
level_19.hint: The thief takes every pair of boots you carry. Look for a way past him before you need your boots again.

level_20.title: Customs
level_20.hint: A barrier stops you while you carry the item it shows. Spend the key first, and let the thief lighten your load.

level_21.title: Light Fingers
level_21.hint: This thief takes every key you carry, green ones too. Open what you can before you cross him, and find another way back.

level_22.title: Stepping Stones
level_22.hint: A turtle carries you across the water once, then dives. Each turtle bridge works one way only: choose the first one with care.

level_23.title: Hot Swap
level_23.hint: The orange button switches every flame jet: lit ones go out, cold ones light up. Check the next row before you press.

level_24.title: Contraband
level_24.hint: Turtles, flames and a customs barrier. A turtle you step back from is gone, so cross in one go. Spend the red key before you head for the exit.

level_25.title: Spending Spree
level_25.hint: Two blue keys, three blue doors. Look into every wing before you open one: only one order reaches the yellow key.

level_26.title: Cold Storage
level_26.hint: Blocks slide on ice and turn at curved corners, just like you. Follow each block path to the water before you push.

level_27.title: Countdown
level_27.hint: Two teeth hunt you and the clock is short. Stopwatches add ten seconds: grab them on the way.

level_28.title: Hideouts
level_28.hint: Creatures cannot cross blue walls, but a blue wall you walk through is gone for good. Once a hideout is open, they can follow you in.

level_29.title: Open Air
level_29.hint: Gliders circle the edge of the plaza. Each wing gives the key to the next one: red, then blue, then yellow. In the west wing, park a block on the brown button before you step on the trap.

level_30.title: Epoxy Core
level_30.hint: Everything you learned, one wing at a time. The green key opens both green doors, but the thief at the east wing takes it: open them before you go there.

keys_doors.title: Locksmith Run #{number}
keys_doors.hint: Each colored door eats a key of its color. Green keys open every green door.

fire.title: Ember Crossing #{number}
fire.hint: Fire burns without fire boots. Look for them before you step in.

water.title: Flooded Halls #{number}
water.hint: Water drowns you without flippers. Grab them first.

blocks_water.title: Bridge Builders #{number}
blocks_water.hint: Push a block into water to turn it into dirt you can walk on. Plan the push before you move.

ice.title: Glacier Drift #{number}
ice.hint: Ice keeps you sliding until something stops you. Corners turn your slide.

force.title: Conveyor Works #{number}
force.hint: Force floors carry you along. Force boots let you walk against them.

thief.title: Thieves' Den #{number}
thief.hint: The thief takes all your boots. Use them before you meet him.

toggle_walls.title: Switchyard #{number}
toggle_walls.hint: Every green button flips every toggle wall. Count your presses.

trap.title: Bear Trap Alley #{number}
trap.hint: A bear trap holds you until its brown button is pressed. A block can keep the button down.

teleport.title: Quantum Hop #{number}
teleport.hint: Step on a teleporter to come out of another one, moving the same way. With several pads, the order you use them matters.

sokoban.title: Warehouse #{number}
sokoban.hint: Every brown button holds a trap open. Push a block onto each button, and never into a corner.

monsters.title: Creature Feature #{number}
monsters.hint: Monsters follow fixed patterns. Watch them, wait for the gap, then move.

bomb.title: Demolition Run #{number}
bomb.hint: Bombs blow up anything that touches them. Push a block into one to clear the way.

cloner.title: Clone Works #{number}
cloner.hint: A red button makes the clone machine drop a copy of its block. Clone as many blocks as the job needs.

dirt.title: Excavation #{number}
dirt.hint: Blocks cannot cross dirt or fake blue walls until you clear them on foot. Clear the right path before you push.

default.hint: Use the Objective button (or H) to locate the next mechanism and inspect trap, cloner, and toggle links.

1.title: Foundations
1.subtitle: Chips, keys, boots, ice and force floors.

2.title: Mechanisms
2.subtitle: Buttons, traps, bombs, teleporters and thin walls.

3.title: Creatures
3.subtitle: Bugs, tanks, hidden walls and clone machines.

4.title: Contraband
4.subtitle: Thieves, item barriers, turtles and flame jets.

5.title: Core
5.subtitle: Gold keys, bonus clocks and fast hunters, all together.

level_1.title: Power Up
level_1.hint: Collect every chip to open the socket, then step through the exit.

level_2.title: Four Pens
level_2.hint: A thin wall closes only one edge of a square, so check which side of each pen is open before you walk in.

level_3.title: Two Doors, Two Keys
level_3.hint: A red key opens one red door and then disappears, so spend each key on the door right after it.

level_4.title: The Two Attics
level_4.hint: Think before you open a door, and if you get stuck press U to undo a step or R to restart.

level_5.title: The Greenhouse Keeper
level_5.hint: A green key is never used up: one key opens every green door.

level_6.title: Footprints
level_6.hint: Dirt turns into floor once you step on it, so the dirt that is left shows where you have not been yet.

level_7.title: Printed Circuit
level_7.hint: The socket opens when its counter reaches zero.

level_8.title: The Cheapest Basket
level_8.hint: The counter shows how many chips the socket still needs, not how many lie on the board, so you do not have to take them all.

level_9.title: The Socket Door
level_9.hint: The socket is not always the last gate: look at what lies behind it before you count on the exit.

level_10.title: The Key Ring
level_10.hint: A red door eats the key that opens it: count keys before opening a room without one.

level_11.title: The Hedge
level_11.hint: A key you keep is worth more than the steps you save.

level_12.title: The Orchard
level_12.hint: The socket asks for six chips, not all nine: work out which rooms you really need before a red key opens one.

level_13.title: Zen Garden
level_13.hint: Nothing in this garden can lock you out, so take the chips in any order and enjoy the walk.

level_14.title: Two Key Rings
level_14.hint: A key can hide behind a door of the other colour: trace the chain backwards to find the one lock everything else hangs from.

level_15.title: The Clockmaker
level_15.hint: A spent key is gone for good: before opening a door, check that the keys still out of reach can pay for what remains.

level_16.title: The Bends
level_16.hint: Walking into a block pushes it one cell, so slide each block into a free cell beside your way to clear the corridor.

level_17.title: The Ford
level_17.hint: Water drowns you, but a block pushed into it fills the pool.

level_18.title: The Rails
level_18.hint: Cover every target with a block to win, there is no exit, and a block only moves straight ahead of you.

level_19.title: Dead Ends
level_19.hint: Before you push, look where the block will stop: in a corner, along a wall with no target or squeezed in a square, it can never move again.

level_20.title: The Trodden Bridge
level_20.hint: A two-wide river needs two blocks in the same row, and fresh dirt stops a block until you have walked over it.

level_21.title: The Embankment
level_21.hint: A block sunk in the river leaves a bridge, but a bridge only helps a block that travels in the row of its target.

level_22.title: Tidying Up
level_22.hint: Every block lies a few pushes from its target: cover all the targets to win, in whatever order you like.

level_23.title: The Metronome
level_23.hint: A pink ball runs straight along its corridor and turns back at a wall, and a block stops it: it can neither cross one nor push it.

level_24.title: The Crossing
level_24.hint: A pink ball never steps on gravel, and a block between you and the ball keeps it away from you.

level_25.title: The Workshop
level_25.hint: A block that stops above an empty target is stuck for good once another block rests on it, so fill a bay from the bottom.

level_26.title: The Doorkeeper
level_26.hint: A key opens one door and is spent, a block cannot pass a closed door, and fresh dirt stops a block until you have walked on it.

level_27.title: Don't Dig
level_27.hint: A pink ball runs straight until something stops it, and dirt stops it. Walk through that dirt and the ball runs on.

level_28.title: Four Splashes
level_28.hint: A block pushed into water sinks and leaves dirt you can walk on: one block, one pool.

level_29.title: The Lock
level_29.hint: Every pool and every pink ball you must stop costs one block, and a block spent on another job is gone. A pink ball cannot pass a block.

level_30.title: The Great Works
level_30.hint: Cover every target to win. A block fills a pool or covers a target, never both. A block on the top or bottom row can never leave it, so send each of those rows exactly two blocks.

level_31.title: Firewall
level_31.hint: Fire burns you unless you wear fire boots. Look for the boots at the end of the corridor, then walk through the flames.

level_32.title: A Block for the Flippers
level_32.hint: Flippers let you walk through water, but a moat guards them and you have a single block. Use it on the moat: once the flippers are on your feet, no other water needs a block.

level_33.title: Slide
level_33.hint: Ice carries you until you reach solid ground, and a wall only sends you back. Slide along every corridor to collect all the chips.

level_34.title: Toboggan
level_34.hint: A bent ice tile turns your slide. Follow each track with your eyes: one ends beside the exit, so ride it last.

level_35.title: Key on the Fly
level_35.hint: A key lying on the ice is picked up as you slide over it, and a door opens as you slide into it with its key. Slide down the lane with the key to reach the door.

level_36.title: Delivery
level_36.hint: Ice carries a block the way it carries you, and a block that sinks in water leaves dirt you can walk on. Do not step on the ice yourself: you would slide into the water. Push the block into the corridor and let it slide in.

level_37.title: The Bug
level_37.hint: A bug follows the wall on its left hand and cannot cross dirt. Step on the dirt and step back: the way you open leads the bug straight into the pool.

level_38.title: Thaw
level_38.hint: A block of ice turns a fire into water, and a block of dirt fills that water. Push the ice into the flames first, then bring the dirt: the other way round, the dirt jams the fire for good.

level_39.title: Alchemy
level_39.hint: A fire takes an ice block first and a dirt block after it, a water takes a dirt block, and a block sent at the wrong hazard is lost for good. Count your blocks, and walk over the fresh dirt before the next block comes. Only one block may be in the lane at a time.

level_40.title: The Brake
level_40.hint: Ice carries you on, but a fire cell stops you if you wear the fire boots, and a water cell stops you if you wear the flippers. Wear the right boots to stop on the right cell: without them the slide ends in the flames or the water.

level_41.title: Melt and Swim
level_41.hint: A block of ice turns a fire into water, and flippers let you swim across that water: no dirt block is needed. Fetch the flippers first, cross the lake, then push the ice down its shaft and along the corridor into the flames. Pushed up against the wall, it is stuck.

level_42.title: Roller Coaster
level_42.hint: Ride the ice track in one go: its bends carry you over all five chips. The track crosses itself, and whichever end you start from, you pick them all up.

1.title: Pilot foundations
1.subtitle: The first levels of the rebuilt campaign.

level_1.title: Amber Vein
level_1.hint: Dirt stops a boulder until you clear it. Leave the upper dirt untouched until you are ready to push the boulder South across the water trench.

level_2.title: The Buried Sluice
level_2.hint: A two-cell water trench needs two boulders in the same column. Sink the eastern boulder first, then bring the western one across to reach the red key.

level_3.title: Twin Vaults
level_3.hint: Bridge the central pool with the boulder to claim the red key, then unlock the red and blue vaults in chain to recover the green key.

level_4.title: Sandstone Siphon
level_4.hint: Each upper vault is guarded by a water trench. Push one boulder West and the other East to bridge both trenches and recover the two keys.

level_5.title: The Crimson Counterweight
level_5.hint: The red hold door stays open only while a boulder rests on the red pressure plate. Bridge the western trench for the red key, and park the eastern boulder on the plate.

level_6.title: The Recessed Boulder
level_6.hint: A boulder sitting in a wall recess cannot be pushed from behind. Pick up the Grappling Gloves to pull it South out of its alcove and push it onto the blue plate.

level_7.title: Dual Equilibrium
level_7.hint: Two hold doors guard the exit shaft, and both boulders start inside northern wall recesses. Use the Grappling Gloves to pull each boulder out, then loop around to push them onto the red and blue plates.

level_8.title: The Pit Exchange
level_8.hint: Push the western boulder North into the water to reach the Grappling Gloves, then pull the eastern boulder out of its recess and guide it onto the yellow pressure plate.

level_9.title: The Buried Beam
level_9.hint: Dirt blocks a laser beam until you dig it away, and a slash mirror turns an East-bound beam North. Push the mirror into the beam line to light the red receiver and clear the eastern passage.

level_10.title: Retractable Prism
level_10.hint: The central wall shields the eastern wing from the laser beam. Use the Grappling Gloves to pull the recessed mirror down the safe eastern corridor, then push it into the beam.

level_11.title: Crossed Refraction
level_11.hint: Route the beam around the central pillar with two mirrors: position the upper backslash mirror first so it turns a North-bound beam West into the receiver, then push the lower slash mirror into the emitter line.

level_12.title: Heart of the Sanctuary
level_12.hint: Combine every tool of the sanctuary: push the slash mirror North to light the red laser receiver, and use the Grappling Gloves in the eastern wing to extract the recessed boulder and weigh down the blue plate.

level_13.title: Two-Wing Necropolis
level_13.hint: Bridge the western water trench with a boulder to recover the red key, weigh down the eastern blue pressure plate with the second boulder, then bridge the upper pool with the third boulder to reach the exit.

level_14.title: Twin Pull Halls
level_14.hint: Pick up the Grappling Gloves and pull both western boulders out of their top and bottom recesses onto the red and blue plates, then bridge the eastern trench with the third boulder to claim the red key.

level_15.title: Winged Dual Sanctuary
level_15.hint: Walk up the inner side aisles to collect the upper chips first, then push the outer boulders South into both water trenches to claim the red and blue keys, and park the central boulder on the yellow pressure plate.

level_16.title: Lagoon of Six Bridges
level_16.hint: Push one western boulder South through the narrow canal to bridge the southwest trench, park the second western boulder on the blue plate, then bridge the three eastern trenches in sequence to unlock the exit.

level_17.title: Cruciform Hall of Scrolls
level_17.hint: Take the Grappling Gloves in the southern wing to pull the recessed boulder North and push it onto the yellow plate, then pull both northern boulders out of their alcoves onto the red and blue plates.

level_18.title: Chambers of Rebirth
level_18.hint: Weigh down the red and blue plates in the lower vault to open the central shaft, collect the upper chips while staying clear of the beam, then push the slash mirror North to light the red laser receiver.

level_19.title: River Vault of Prisms
level_19.hint: Bridge the western trench to recover the Grappling Gloves, pull the south-central boulder out to bridge the eastern trench, then pull the upper slash mirror East out of its alcove before pushing the second mirror into the beam.

level_20.title: Pyramid of Harmony
level_20.hint: Collect the southern chips and Grappling Gloves first, push the slash mirror North into the beam to open the red laser gate, weigh down the eastern blue plate, and pull the northern boulder South into the central water trench.

2.title: Counterweights & Grappling
2.subtitle: Pressure plates, hold doors and the Grappling Gloves.

3.title: Subterranean Optics
3.subtitle: Buried laser emitters, sliding prisms and sanctuary gates.

4.title: Guardian Temples
